correctness.rationale: The rank-one formula is derived from a two-dimensional quadratic form, the tuple norm from its common source, and two symmetric unit test vectors force 4W²≥A²+s1². The singular-value trace bound produces the quantified inequality. Equality when q>1 forces A=0 and q equal positive singular values; the t-variation excludes A>0 when q=1. Orthogonal-source singular vectors give a matching upper bound and explicit witnesses for every m,k over R and C. Finite exact and random checks from verify.py agree but do not replace these analytic quantifiers.

originality.rationale: The key new statement is k≥m saturation for the common-source rank-one class, along with full extremizer classification and an exact spectral defect. Mal 2022/2023 treats unrestricted complex indices only for k<m in finite dimension. Grover–Singla 2022 treats subgradients, not this index. An inaccessible early construction paper and possible unindexed equivalents remain real risks.

value.rationale: This is the exact restricted extremum for the natural construction underlying Mal’s sharp Hilbert theorem, not a fabricated coordinate slice. It identifies a genuine dimensional phase boundary and the rigid transition from orthogonal outputs to tight frames. The spectral defect bounds source leakage and failure of equal singular values for nearly minimal tuples, a structural quantitative use beyond mere reproducibility.
